`retrieval_recall_at_k` is the fraction of relevant documents found within the first k retrieved; `retrieval_mrr` is the reciprocal rank of the first relevant document within the first k, 0 if none. The engine reports them at fixed cut-offs (`EngineConfig.recall_ks`, default 1 and 3, and `mrr_k`, default 3) as `retrieval_recall_at_1`, `retrieval_recall_at_3` and `retrieval_mrr_at_3`. A fixed K matters: an un-cut recall compares a system that retrieves one document with one that retrieves three, which is how the old report credited idf weighting with a gain that came from K. Repeated ids count once, and a case with an empty retrieval scores 0 instead of dropping out of the mean. Ground truth is declarative: each `EvalCase` lists `supporting_doc_ids`, the documents that should be retrieved for that input. `retrieval_metrics.py` is short on purpose. The honest difficulty in retrieval evaluation is constructing reliable ground truth for real corpora, and the module docstring says the project does not pretend to have solved that. For the demo, the {{ds.n_docs}}-document corpus makes hand-labelling feasible.
